1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output, __wherein the database operation predictor comprises an estimated Central Processing Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation or an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by the one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation__; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein inputting further includes inputting the database constructs as query execution plans for a query.

3. (Previously presented) The method of claim 2, wherein inputting further includes identifying at least one database construct as a least cost query execution plan identified from the query execution plans by the database optimizer.

4. (Previously presented) The method of claim 3, wherein identifying further includes identifying individual pieces of the least cost query execution plan as: a total number of spools used, cardinality for tables with any intermediate results used, a total number of merge joins, a total number of hash joins, nested loop joins, references for the spools, and costs per database resource assigned by the database optimizer.

5. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation.

6. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (1/O) operations performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for the database operation as the modified database construct.

8. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for execution of a query as the modified database construct.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct.

10. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs.

11. (Original) The method of claim 10 further comprising, rendering an interface from the database statistics depicting relationships between the database operation, the database operation predictor, the database constructs, and the modified database construct with respect to other instances of the database operation, other database operation predictors, other database constructs, and other modified database constructs.

12. (Currently amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query based on the least cost query execution plan, __wherein the predicted execution time comprises an estimated Central Processing Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute the query or an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by the one or more Access Module Processors during execution of the query__; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising, notifying a database administrator when based on the predicted execution time a Service Level Goal (SLG) or Service Level Agreement (SLA) associated with the query will be unable to be satisfied using the least cost query execution plan or using a modified version of the least cost query execution plan that was modified based on the predicted execution time.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising: providing an interface rendered through a database tool that models the database constructs, the query execution plans, an actual query execution time for the query, and the predicted execution time for the query against other queries having other database constructs, other query execution plans, other actual query execution times for the other queries, and other predicted execution times provided by the machine-learning algorithm for the other queries.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim [[15]] __14__, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system.

16. (Previously presented) The method of claim 12, wherein training further includes training the machine-learning algorithm as a linear regression-based machine-learning algorithm.

17. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes selecting a different one of the query execution plans to execute the query instead of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted execution time and a historical actual execution time known for the different query execution plan.

18. (Previously presented) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time and a current performance associated with the execution resource.

19. (Currently amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation, __wherein the predicted value comprises an estimated Central Processing Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute the database operation or an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by the one or more Access Module Processors during execution of the database operation__; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predict value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system.

20. (Currently amended) The system of claim 19, wherein the predicted value is an estimated query execution time for a query __for the one or more Access Module Processors__ and the database operation is execution of a query execution plan for the query within the database management system.
